claim_text: 83-98% of agricultural CV papers do not report calibration metrics such as ECE, reliability diagrams, Brier score, or confidence curves.
scope: methodology: calibration reporting in agri-CV literature
evidence_locations: outputs/method_gap_matrix.csv, column: calibration_reported (52 papers: 46 no, 2 partial, 0 yes across original 46; 2 partial in new)
contradictory_evidence: None identified. 0 papers scored `yes` across the 46-paper sample.
uncertainty: medium — 2 papers now show partial calibration
required_validation: manual audit of 10 randomly sampled papers to confirm no calibration mentioned outside extraction context
notes: Single partial mention found (not full calibration).

claim_text: 48-91% of agricultural CV papers lack strong simple baselines (varies by tagging scheme).
contradictory_evidence: 4 papers with `strong_simple` tag: Outdoor Plant Seg (RF+CNN), Multimodal Disease Benchmark (RF+DT), two others
uncertainty: high — tagging differences between scoring runs
required_validation: confirm the 4 `strong_simple` papers actually used non-DL baselines with parity parameterization

claim_text: 71-79% of agricultural CV papers use random/unclear splits risking field/plant leakage.
contradictory_evidence: 10 papers with grouped splits: 1 grouped_field, 4 grouped_plant, 3 grouped_location, 1 grouped_time
uncertainty: low — split description is usually explicit in methodology
required_validation: verify grouped-split papers actually enforce held-out field/plant identity rather than random tiles

claim_text: 87% of agricultural CV papers evaluate on same sensor only.
contradictory_evidence: 10 papers test cross-dataset; no paper tests cross-sensor explicitly
uncertainty: medium — cross-sensor vs cross-dataset distinction may be ambiguous in some papers
required_validation: manually check `cross_dataset` papers for any implicit cross-sensor evaluation

claim_text: 54-59% of agricultural CV papers release no code.
uncertainty: low — code availability is binary from paper text
required_validation: spot-check 5 `not_available` papers for supplementary material with code

claim_text: 69% of agricultural CV papers exhibit 4+ simultaneous methodological gaps.
scope: methodology: cumulative methodology weakness in agri-CV
uncertainty: medium — gap thresholds are somewhat arbitrary (4 of 6 dimensions)
required_validation: verify 4 low-gap papers on each dimension manually
notes: Updated from 33/46 (72%) at 46 papers to 36/52 (69%) at 52 papers

claim_text: AgroVG (22), PhenoBench (21), and AgroTools (20.5) lead opportunity scores among 30 datasets.
contradictory_evidence: Weeds-Banana (19.5), WE3DS (19.5), CropNet (20) — close alternatives with different modality trade-offs
uncertainty: medium — scores reflect agent judgment per rubric, not exhaustive review
required_validation: human review of AgroVG paper and dataset access; replicate scoring on top 5
notes: PhenoBench and AgroTools added; AgroVG remains rank 1

claim_text: PhenoBench scores 21/25 (rank 2) with exceptional annotation depth (2000+ hrs, 5 tasks) but moderate feasibility (same-sensor test only).
uncertainty: medium — license requires verification beyond paper text
required_validation: verify CropNet license and access mechanism

claim_text: Multimodal/3D datasets (CropNet, WE3DS, Crops3D, PLANesT-3D, TomatoWUR, AgriLiRa4D) cluster at the top of opportunity rankings (19-20), suggesting non-RGB modalities are the highest-value research target.
uncertainty: medium — small sample (27 datasets), agent scoring correlations not controlled
required_validation: re-score after full 260-paper corpus; indicate which modalities each dataset has been tested on
